title: Health Endpoint

validation.research: Seven primary references: Chris Richardson catalogs Health Check API; Microsoft describes Health Endpoint Monitoring and its external observer, depth, cost, staleness and security; Kubernetes defines startup/liveness/readiness decisions and startup gating; Spring Boot documents dependency-selection risks, main versus management paths and lifecycle health state; AWS ALB documents all-unhealthy fail-open routing; Python documents WSGI/reference-server limits; RFC 9111 defines no-store. Health Check API is the interface catalog name and Health Endpoint Monitoring describes the endpoint/observer collaboration. These are searchable names for the pattern family, with scope explained. Original order-service situation, injected Boolean policy, loopback HTTP experiment and native figures.

runnable_example.verification: Actual article fences run unchanged on Python 3.11+. Real ephemeral loopback HTTP requests produce all five exact output rows and match every lifecycle figure value. WSGI validation middleware verifies the app/server boundary. All eight Boolean state combinations are tested over GET and HEAD: liveness never reads the dependency snapshot, startup tracks initialization, readiness requires initialization plus dependency and excludes draining, and stateful requests read one snapshot. HEAD has empty body with matching content-length semantics. Unsupported methods return 405/Allow without consulting state, unknown paths return 404, query strings do not echo private values, and ordinary responses use minimal fixed bodies and no-store. A broken provider propagates its exact error through the app and becomes HTTP 500 at the server, without a green fallback or diagnostic disclosure; shallow liveness remains independent. Responses close, listeners close and server threads are shut down/joined with inventory returning to baseline. No real dependency verification, freshness enforcement, business handler, production server, authentication/TLS, observer/controller, routing removal, restart action or complete deadline is inferred.

example_limits: New canonical Health Endpoint article. Health Check API is Richardson’s interface catalog name; Health Endpoint Monitoring names endpoint plus observer in Microsoft’s catalog. These are searchable names for the pattern family. Original order-service situation and Python 3.11+ WSGI application plus real loopback HTTP experiment. The trusted snapshot callback atomically returns initialized/dependency_ok/draining Boolean state without remote I/O. Live returns 200 only when this request loop can answer and does not read dependency state; startup reflects initialization; readiness requires initialization, the selected required dependency and not draining. GET/HEAD are supported, other methods return 405 with Allow, unknown paths return 404, and minimal responses carry no-store. Five stable phases produce 200/503/503, 200/200/200, 200/200/503, 200/200/200 and 200/200/503. All routes are called directly in the demo; startup-gated observers normally suppress other probes until startup succeeds. The server binds an ephemeral loopback port, bypasses proxies, closes each response, and is shut down/joined/closed by its owner. No real dependency checker, aged-state enforcement, business handler, controller, routing/restart action, TLS, authentication, complete deadline or production HTTP server is supplied. Independent requests may straddle changes, and readiness loss is not a universal no-traffic guarantee. Actual HTTP tests cover every Boolean state combination, one snapshot per stateful request, no liveness dependency access, GET/HEAD parity, unsupported-method and route failures, no-store/minimal bodies, provider failure becoming HTTP 500 and complete owned cleanup. The snapshot is trusted injected evidence, not a dependency check or stale-state control. No business path, route controller, restart controller or universal traffic-removal guarantee is implemented.
